teams.heading: Fiji concede 14 penalties to lose Pacific Nations Cup final against Japan
teams.body: Fiji surrendered their Pacific Nations Cup title in Saturday's final in Tokyo, falling 20-15 to Japan after a collapse in discipline and set-piece execution. Despite leading 12-10 at half-time through tries from Virimi Vakatawa and captain Tevita Ikanivere, the Flying Fijians fell apart after the interval. Fiji finished with just 36 per cent possession, missed 24 tackles and conceded 14 penalties. Halfback Frank Lomani admitted second-half mistakes allowed the hosts back into the contest as Samisoni Tua scored the late decider.

lead.why: Japan defeated Fiji 20-15 in the Pacific Nations Cup final on Saturday to claim the title.

teams.heading: England draw with Canada to end their historic 39-game winning run
teams.body: England's historic 39-match winning streak came to an end after a thrilling 26-26 draw against Canada at Sandy Park. John Mitchell's side were undone by a loose late carry and a crucial late turnover, having earlier relied on a Claudia Moloney-MacDonald brace to fight back. Despite Bryony Field's second-half try, Canada's relentless physical pressure secured the draw. The result represents the first time England have failed to win since the 2022 World Cup final.

teams.heading: France women overcome extraordinary six-card chaos to beat Australia in Aix-en-Provence
teams.body: France women staged an astonishing second-half comeback to defeat Australia 29-26 on Saturday, despite being reduced to 11 players at one stage. Playing in Aix-en-Provence—where a burning bus outside the stadium delayed the second half—the hosts fell 19-0 behind after receiving a red card and three yellows. Although a sixth card followed after the interval, Pauline Bourdon Sansus scored a crucial try as the hosts reeled off 17 unanswered points in the final 25 minutes to seal an unlikely victory.

teams.heading: Ireland surrender 19 point lead to lose WXV opener against USA
teams.body: A second-half disciplinary collapse saw Ireland surrender a 19-point lead in Sunday's WXV opener, losing 40-36 to the United States in Dublin. After cruising to a 31-12 advantage, a pivotal yellow card for Vicky Elmes Kinlan allowed the visitors to score four unanswered tries and snatch victory. Head coach Scott Bemand lamented his side's inability to halt their opponents' power game, stressing they 'need to get 80-minute performances' ahead of facing Japan.

lead.why: Ireland's shock second-half collapse and defeat against the USA in the WXV opener is the day's dominant story.

teams.heading: Italy captain Vittoria Ostuni Minuzzi celebrates 50th cap in Japan rout
teams.body: The Azzurre launched their WXV Global Series campaign with a commanding 55-21 victory over Japan at Stadio Omero Tognon. Captain Vittoria Ostuni Minuzzi celebrated her 50th cap with a second-half try as Italy racked up their highest-ever points tally against the Sakura XV. Despite a brief Japanese fightback, the hosts responded with three quick first-half tries in seven minutes from Alyssa D'Inca, Vittoria Vecchini, and Giordana Duca to regain control and secure a dominant opening win.

teams.heading: Mark Jones explains Ospreys' Australian recruitment drive born of board "necessity"
teams.body: Ospreys head coach Mark Jones has addressed the club’s summer influx of Australian talent, including Wallabies Liam Wright and Marika Koroibete. Jones told the Scrum V podcast that recruiting heavily from the Southern Hemisphere was a "necessity" after board approval for signings was delayed until May. Following the departures of Jac Morgan and Dewi Lake, the region targeted players from the same area to aid squad cohesion. He believes these "quality" arrivals will prove vital in supporting homegrown development throughout the 2026-27 campaign.

teams.heading: Les Kiss recalls Jordan Petaia to Wallabies squad following NFL injury misdiagnosis
teams.body: Head coach Les Kiss has handed Jordan Petaia an international lifeline, naming the utility back in his latest 34-man squad. Petaia returns following a brief, injury-marred stint with the NFL’s Los Angeles Chargers, where a misdiagnosed hamstring tendon issue cut his American football ambitions short. Having proved his fitness in the Top 14 with Perpignan, the 26-year-old is now prioritising a role in the 2027 World Cup cycle after last appearing for Australia during the 2023 tournament.

teams.heading: Japan reclaim Pacific Nations Cup title after Samisoni Tua sinks holders Fiji
teams.body: Japan secured their first Pacific Nations Cup title since 2019 with a 20-15 victory over holders Fiji at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium on Saturday. After trailing 12-10 at half-time despite Mamoru Harada's effort, the Brave Blossoms rallied through a Ben Gunter try before Samisoni Tua crossed in the final 10 minutes to clinch the trophy. The result lifts Eddie Jones' side to ninth in the world rankings. Captain Naoto Saito hailed the victory as a "trigger for us to break through and create new history."

lead.why: Japan's victory in the Pacific Nations Cup final is the dominant story across all rugby outlets today.

teams.heading: Shane Howarth urges New Zealand Rugby to scrap overseas eligibility rules
teams.body: Despite an unbeaten Nations Championship start, former All Black Shane Howarth insists New Zealand must abandon its ban on overseas-based players to rescue a declining scrum. Following a 3-1 series loss to South Africa, Howarth backed the coaching staff’s assessment that the departure of South African franchises from Super Rugby has left local props under-prepared. "You’re not going to get an argument from me," Howarth said regarding the need to mirror the Springboks' open selection policy to bridge the physicality gap.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus releases Pieter-Steph du Toit and Damian de Allende early
teams.body: Coach Rassie Erasmus has released flanker Pieter-Steph du Toit and centre Damian de Allende from the squad ahead of next Sunday’s one-off Test against the Wallabies in Perth. The pair will return home to South Africa to spend time with their families following a demanding workload during the recent series against the All Blacks. Erasmus confirmed there is sufficient cover within the current travelling group to manage the rotation as the team prepares for the upcoming fixture at Optus Stadium.
